title: First show ideas
summary: Names Ben Taylor as presenter and Maxie Haddow-Allen as producer. Considers charity-shop records, punk, psychedelia, live poetry, acoustic sessions, and a theme tune.

title: The Ben Taylor Show
summary: The November proposal puts the show at 1–3am and imagines regular Aztec Camera records, Pijnacker news, local poets, and songs played at the wrong speed.

title: Names for the show
summary: Possible titles include ‘How to leave the planet’ and ‘Shambling Rank Amateurism’. One feature starts with the phone box outside the station.

title: A two-hour demo
summary: Theme candidates include the London Symphony Orchestra’s ‘Whole Lotta Love’, a Hammond version of ‘King of the Road’, and ‘Popcorn’.

title: After the demo
summary: The team reviews microphone technique, the links, levels, and how much space to leave after a performance. Ben volunteers to drop ‘a word from our sponsors’.

title: Making room for Rufus
summary: Budgets eight minutes for a poet, twelve for a musician, four for trivia, and four for different versions of one song at the end.

title: The original website copy
summary: Draft listing for a ninety-minute show with live sessions, poetry, psychedelia, garage, folk, and charity-shop kitsch. It closes ‘Dead, dead good.’

title: Time check! Tea break!
summary: A Batman-style refrain has variants for a time check, a tea break, the phone-in, and the end of the show. Other lines include ‘Dead Air is filmed in front of a live studio audience’.

title: Notes on the presentation
summary: Four lines of feedback on voice, Rufus, variety in the record introductions, and the short stories.

title: The first February rehearsal sheet
summary: Aztec Camera, the Clash, and Paul Simon open the record sequence. Readings with a Klaus Wunderlich backing are marked as replacements for session slots.

title: A second February rehearsal sheet
summary: The Clash open the music; the sheet leaves spaces for five new tunes. ‘Popcorn’ returns after the news.

title: First Sunday, 16 February
summary: Ninety minutes with Eoin Quiery sessions, readings, trivia, and a disc played at two speeds. Cue times run from 16:00 to 17:30.

title: Catweazle performers
summary: The production folder contains a working directory of local musicians and poets.

title: Katie Buckhaven, 23 February
summary: Three songs for Katie Buckhaven, with a phone-booth song by Primitive Radio Gods near the close.

title: The links and the silences
summary: Ben and Rufus dialogue, jingles, and instructions for a deliberate five-second silence. The document footer gives 16 February.

title: George Kirby and Dave Dwan, 2 March
summary: George’s live songs share a running order with Dave Dwan, Professor Pea, and records from Lord Tanamo to Jeff Buckley.

title: The revised rehearsal sheet
summary: A version of the news, records, and readings format with a ‘BT/FS’ footer. The filename and revised save date cannot date any broadcast.

title: An early Dylan note
summary: A short note pairs Bowie’s ‘Song For Bob Dylan’ with a Simon & Garfunkel song about Dylan.

title: Unclassified and Andreas, 9 March
summary: A list of session, poetry, feature, and disc entries for the programme, including Julian Dickinson and Julia Middleton as Unclassified.

title: Unclassified and Andreas, at the desk
summary: A timed version of the 9 March show with Rufus on the microphones, three Unclassified slots, Andreas, Professor Pea, and Uncle Anton.

title: Extra time, 16 March
summary: The tracks and features for an extended show include Superfly, Sam, Kenickie on tape, and Ghostface Killah.

title: The extended Sunday at the desk
summary: The extra half-hour takes the show through to 17:58. The closing stretch includes ‘The Killing Moon’ by Echo and the Bunnymen.

title: April reading sheet
summary: A collection of texts in capitals. No aired sequence or performer is established by the file.

title: April music choices
summary: Eoin’s songs sit with the Cadillacs, the Champs, Jan & Dean, and Gorky’s Zygotic Mynci. Some entries carry disc and track numbers; there is no complete on-air sequence.

title: More April music choices
summary: The list marks individual selections and names ‘Machine Gun’ by the Commodores as a music bed.

title: April links and readings
summary: Surreal compliments, other reading material, and a link about playing back a message.

title: Reading research
summary: A text attributed within the file to a published translation. The file alone does not establish that a reading was broadcast.

title: The Dylan show script
summary: Notes for the penultimate show bring together Eoin Quiery, George Kirby, and Dylan Bedford. The script also casts the Boo Boys and stages an interview.

title: Dylan cover versions, 8 June
summary: Commercial recordings and live options appear separately. The latter include two Eoin songs and a ten-minute slot for George’s ‘Sad Eyed Lady of the Lowlands’.

title: June music and returning features
summary: A 15 June file lists Jonathan Richman, Robert Wyatt, the Smiths, and the phone box outside the station.
